basis.title: CNA e-Tool Estimated Useful Life Table
basis.by: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
basis.label: Electric heat pump, condenser, pad or rooftop
basis.note: Same life for family and elderly properties. US multifamily housing. HUD's row also covers split-system heat pump condensers on a pad.

basis.title: Energy Conservation Program: Energy Conservation Standards for Air Cooled, Three-Phase, Small Commercial Air Conditioners and Heat Pumps With a Cooling Capacity of Less Than 65,000 Btu/h (NOPR), 87 FR 18290, March 30, 2022
basis.label: "the average lifetimes of 19 years for air conditioners and 16.2 years for heat pumps"
basis.note: Printed page 18300. class: three-phase commercial heat pumps <65,000 Btu/h (single-package and split). Carried over from the September 2020 NODA/RFI. Proposed rule, not final.

basis.title: Energy Conservation Program: Energy Conservation Standards for Air-Cooled Commercial Package Air Conditioners and Heat Pumps (direct final rule), 89 FR 44052, May 20, 2024
basis.label: Equipment Lifetime: "DOE assumed a mean lifetime of 21 years for small equipment classes"
basis.note: Printed page 44092. class: small ACUAC/ACUHP (>=65,000 and <135,000 Btu/h), air conditioners and heat pumps alike. Carried over from the January 2016 DFR (which gave 21.1 years). Also in the LCC inputs summary table, p.39 (printed 44090).

basis.title: Energy Conservation Program: Energy Conservation Standards for Air-Cooled Commercial Package Air Conditioners and Heat Pumps (direct final rule), 89 FR 44052, May 20, 2024
basis.label: Equipment Lifetime: "a mean lifetime of 23 years for large equipment classes"
basis.note: Printed page 44092. class: large ACUAC/ACUHP (>=135,000 and <240,000 Btu/h). Carried over from the January 2016 DFR (which gave 22.6 years).

basis.title: Energy Conservation Program: Energy Conservation Standards for Air-Cooled Commercial Package Air Conditioners and Heat Pumps (direct final rule), 89 FR 44052, May 20, 2024
basis.label: Equipment Lifetime: "For very large equipment classes, DOE created a new distribution with an assumed mean lifetime of 30 years"
basis.note: Printed page 44092. class: very large ACUAC/ACUHP (>=240,000 and <760,000 Btu/h); new in this rule (2016 DFR used 33.7 years). Very large units are less typical rooftop units.

open_questions: Every source here is a published planning, design or accounting life. None is observed replacement data.
